label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Renee, this is Thu, the owner of Lotus Garden Nails. I am very sorry your toe became red, swollen, and painful, and that you needed urgent care and antibiotics. I truly mean that. I am also sorry if I seemed to shrug when you came back. That was never my intention. I was trying to understand what happened, but I should have shown you more clearly that I cared.

Because this is now public, and people are commenting about the cleanliness of my salon, I would like to explain what happened from our side. I am not calling you a liar, and I do not know what caused your infection. I only ask that our side be heard too.

You came in on Saturday, October 24, for a $45 deluxe pedicure with Vy. Our reusable tools are autoclaved and kept in sealed pouches, and we open the pouch in front of the customer. Files and buffers are new for each person, and you can take yours home. We also use a new plastic liner in the pedicure tub every time. We passed our state inspection in August 2026 with no violations, and the inspection paper is posted on our wall for anyone to see.

Vy is my niece and has been licensed for three years. She was born in Houston and does speak English. She is quiet and shy, especially when she is nervous, but it is not fair to say she barely speaks English. I am sorry if her shyness made it difficult for you to communicate with her.

Vy remembers that during the pedicure, you asked her several times to trim more of the cuticle because you wanted it very clean. She says she told you she did not want to cut too much, and you told her it was fine and that you always did it that way. I was not part of that conversation, so I am sharing what she told me. I am not saying this to blame you for your infection. I only want people to understand that there is more to the service than what has been posted.

When you returned on November 2 and showed me your toe, I offered you the full $45 refund **and** offered to pay your urgent-care copay if you brought me the receipt. The offer was not only $45. I did say no to your request for $300 cash and free pedicures for one year. That was the request I declined. My original offer still stands: I will refund the $45 and pay the urgent-care copay with the receipt.

I have worked in nails in Houston for 19 years. I opened Lotus Garden in 2007 after working for my aunt. In all that time, no customer has ever brought me an infection complaint before this. I am taking your complaint seriously. You said you filed with the state, and I respect your right to do that. We will cooperate fully.

The comments saying that all salons like ours reuse files, have dirty tubs, or are all the same have hurt me deeply. Please judge us by what we actually do. Vy read the forum and cried in our back room. She even told me she wants to quit doing nails. I am not sharing that to make Renee feel guilty, but to ask everyone to remember there are real people behind these comments.

@MarisolB, thank you for being kind and fair, for sharing your own experience, and for suggesting that we talk again. I appreciate that you did that without dismissing Renee’s pain.

Renee, please call me at the salon or come in when you feel comfortable, and we can sit down and talk. I would much rather listen to you directly than continue this through forum comments. I am sorry for what you have gone through, and my offer remains open.
